title: Cheap AI models: who reaches the targets for less money

design.question: With the cheapest model, does an OSO community reach 2 of the targets that count for less money than a traditional one?
design.fixed: four DeepSeek V4.1 Flash labs (two foundation builders, a target racer, a neutral lab), $0.08 each, 12 posted conjectures, up to 30 rounds
design.measure: money spent to solve 2 of the targets that count (A3, X2, B5, A5); a run that never does counts as its whole budget

answer: No clear difference: OSO solved 2 targets that count for $0.27 on average, traditional for $0.27 (1 and 1 of 5 runs got there).
caveats: Budgets were counted at list prices, but OpenRouter charged about 5.6× more ($3.56 against $0.69).
Tests a lead first seen in the earlier cheap-model test, on fresh runs.
One model and one small problem set.
Budgets were not binding: the communities spent 24% of theirs on average, because agents passed.
Values are mean ± standard deviation over runs.
invalid: The money on the key ran out during the test: 950 model calls were refused, so labs stopped early (only 24% of budgets used).
